question: does Pavo's audio binding and lip sync degrade with line or clip length (~>= 8-9 s)? (failed build run 40307414749, k-insight 8.42 s line in a 9 s clip, 0 of 6)
method: direct Pavo calls (0 credits, fresh exact quote each) with episode_build.request()'s exact prompt for each shot, reference storyteller-ref.jpg (ch-keeper-talk, the build's talking reference), seconds = ceil(line); the WAVs rebuilt locally with pilot_render.py voice + episode_build.py lines on plans/genesis-07-short.json (Kokoro v1.0 fp16, pinned sha256); halves cut at the sentence boundary from the same voice.wav and retimed by plan_check.talk_retime/episode_build.retime; every clip judged by lipsync_check.py (thresholds unchanged: audio >= 0.85, mouth >= 0.45, speak/pause >= 1.5, face >= 0.8; face_landmarker sha pinned). 16 generations.

a-insight.text: Notice the order. Grief comes before judgment. The flood is not the story of a cold God, but of a wounded heart.

b-insight-a.text: Notice the order. Grief comes before judgment.
b-insight-a.plan_check: KEEPER_LINE_TOO_SHORT (7 words, under the 12-word rule; ~2.5-3.1 s estimated) and, as a narration line, SHORT INSIGHT_MISSING (no insight line of >= 20 words is left)

b-insight-b.text: The flood is not the story of a cold God, but of a wounded heart.

ctl-line01.prompt: k-insight (control: the E95/E98 tests' WAV under genesis-07's k-insight prompt)

conclusions: length is NOT the cause: the built genesis-07 lines failed at every length, 1 pass in 15 (k-close 6.55 s once); 3.55 s, 4.42 s and 4.55 s lines did no better than the 8.45 s one (audio 0.07-0.98, mouth 0.10-0.47); the halves of the split were the worst (0 of 6)

the same prompt, reference and a 7 s clip with line-01.wav passed at once with the best measures yet (audio 0.992, mouth 0.685, speak/pause 3.24): the service, the prompt (E98 pose) and the reference are fine today; what differs is the input WAV

line-01.wav (the WAV of every passing direct test, E95/E98) has 0.40 s of silence before the first word and 0.75 s after the last (5.24 s of speech in 6.385 s); every WAV episode_build lines writes is cut at the first and last word of its sentences, 0.09-0.14 s of lead and 0.21-0.36 s of tail

in every failing clip Pavo's soundtrack goes on 0.5-1.0 s after our last word up to the end of the clip (the control 0.04 s, but the passing calibration clip keeper-lipsync.mp4 0.96 s too, so that alone does not separate pass from fail); in several failing clips the line is also shifted or stretched (best fit x0.81-0.94 or 0.8-1.0 s off), which never happened with line-01.wav
retiming is not the cause either: the unretimed k-insight and k-insight-b failed like the retimed k-question, k-close and k-insight-a

E95's pad window (0.25-0.65 s from the end of the WAV to the end of the clip) was measured only on line-01.wav, whose own 0.75 s tail and 0.40 s lead were part of what passed: the rule holds on the WAV length, but the words inside it need their silence too (hypothesis H2, not yet tested)
next_test: H2, about 9-12 generations, on k-question (4.08 s of speech) and k-insight (8.14 s): (d) the built WAV with 0.40 s of silence added before the first word and the tail made 0.75 s (line-01's structure), clip = ceil(WAV) with the pad in 0.25-0.65 s; (e) lead silence only; (f) tail silence only; 3 generations each on k-question, then (d) on k-insight (9.3 s WAV, 10 s clip) to see whether length matters once the structure is right. If (d) passes like the control, the fix is in episode_build lines (each talking WAV gets the lead and tail silence, the compose offsets the clip by the lead) with an antidote test, as E103
